name: Autocomplete
explanation: Suggesting matching options in a dropdown as the user types into an input.
requirements: Wait until the user pauses typing before searching (debounce);Move through suggestions with the arrow keys and choose with Enter;Close the list with Escape or when focus leaves the input;Use the combobox pattern with aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant;Show a message when nothing matches
done_when: Suggestions appear quickly, without a request on every keystroke;The whole control works with only the keyboard

name: Form validation
explanation: Checking user input before it is accepted and showing clear error messages next to the fields that need fixing.
triggers: validate;required field;error message;invalid email;form errors;check the input;wrong format;error under;field is wrong;field is invalid;email field
requirements: Show each error next to its field in plain words;Validate when the user leaves a field or submits, not on every keystroke;Keep everything the user typed when showing errors;Link errors to fields with aria-describedby and focus the first error on submit;Validate again on the server;Set aria-invalid=true on fields with errors;Suggest how to fix each error, such as the expected format
done_when: Submitting invalid data shows clear messages and sends nothing;Screen readers read the error for each field;Valid data submits successfully

name: File upload
explanation: Letting users send files to the server, with checks on file size, type and where the files are stored.
triggers: upload;attach a file;profile picture;upload images;send a file
requirements: Check the file type and size in the browser and again on the server;Show upload progress and allow cancelling;Store files outside the web root with generated names;Support drag and drop as well as a normal file picker;Check the real file content (magic bytes) on the server, not only the extension or Content-Type
done_when: Files that are too big or of the wrong type are rejected with a clear message;Uploads up to the maximum size succeed and show progress

name: Date picker
explanation: An input that opens a calendar so users can choose a date or a date range instead of typing it.
triggers: pick a date;choose a date;select a date;calendar;booking dates;date range
requirements: Allow typing the date as well as picking it from the calendar;Show the expected date format, and accept the user's local format;Support arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down to move around the calendar;Prevent, or clearly mark, dates that cannot be chosen;Consider the native input of type date on mobile
done_when: A date can be chosen with only the keyboard;Dates are saved correctly whatever the user's time zone

name: Multi-step form
explanation: A long form split into steps with a progress indicator, letting users go back and forth without losing their answers.
triggers: step by step;multiple steps;next step;long form;progress steps
requirements: Show the steps and where the user is, such as step 2 of 4;Validate each step before moving on, and keep answers when going back;Save progress so a page reload does not lose answers;Move focus to the new step's heading when the step changes;Show a summary to check before the final submit
done_when: Going back and forward never loses any answers;The whole form can be completed with only the keyboard

name: Autosave
explanation: Saving the user's work automatically as they go, so nothing is lost if they close the page or lose their connection.
triggers: save automatically;don't lose;lose my work;save as i type;keep a draft;unsaved changes
requirements: Save when the user pauses typing (debounce) and before leaving the page;Show the save state, such as Saving and All changes saved;Keep a local copy if the network fails, and retry later;Handle edits from another tab or device without silently overwriting them
done_when: Closing the tab right after typing loses nothing;Losing the connection shows a clear message, and saving resumes when it returns

name: Character count
explanation: A message under a text field showing how many characters the user has left before reaching the limit.
triggers: characters left;characters remaining;limit the text length;how many characters;word limit;280 characters;too many characters
requirements: Show how many characters are left, not only the limit;Announce the remaining count to screen readers after a pause in typing, not on every key;Let users type past the limit and show an error, instead of silently cutting the text;Count characters the same way on the client and the server, including emoji;Check the limit on the server too;Warn as the limit gets close, for example at 80 percent
done_when: The count stays accurate while typing and pasting;Text over the limit shows an error instead of being cut off;Screen reader users hear the count without being interrupted on every key

name: Time picker
explanation: An input for choosing a time of day, such as an appointment time, by typing it or picking from a list.
triggers: pick a time;choose a time;select a time;appointment time;time slot;24 hour clock;am or pm
requirements: Let users type the time as well as pick it;Show 12-hour or 24-hour time to match the user's locale;Store times with a clear time zone, or as a local time with the place it applies to;Use steps such as 15 minutes when booking slots;Show times that cannot be chosen as unavailable;Consider the native input of type time on mobile;Label the field and show the expected format
done_when: A time can be entered with only the keyboard;Times are saved and shown correctly across time zones and daylight saving changes

name: Date of birth input
explanation: Three small boxes for day, month and year, used for dates people already know, such as their birthday, instead of a calendar.
synonyms: memorable date;day month year fields;date input fields;birthday field
triggers: date of birth;birthday;dob;birth date;day month and year;expiry date;issue date
requirements: Use separate day, month and year text fields inside a fieldset with a legend;Use inputmode=numeric rather than type=number;Set autocomplete to bday-day, bday-month and bday-year for a birthday;Do not use a calendar picker for dates people know;Accept single digits and month names, such as 3 or March;Say which part is wrong in the error, such as Date of birth must include a year;Check that the date is real and in the past
done_when: Browsers can autofill the date of birth;Invalid dates such as 31 February get a clear error;Screen readers read the legend with each field

name: Input formatting (masks)
explanation: Automatically formatting what the user types, such as adding spaces to a card number or dashes to a phone number.
triggers: format as they type;add dashes;add spaces;format the number;mask the input;card number spacing
requirements: Format the value as the user types without moving the cursor unexpectedly;Accept pasted values with or without separators;Save the raw value, not the formatted one;Show the expected format in a hint, not only as placeholder text;Show a clear error for invalid input instead of blocking typing;Use inputmode to bring up the right mobile keyboard;Check the value again on the server
done_when: Pasting a value with spaces or dashes works;The cursor stays in place when editing the middle of the value;The saved value has no formatting characters

name: Address form
explanation: The fields for entering a postal address, such as for delivery or billing, often with a postcode lookup.
triggers: shipping address;billing address;delivery address;postal address;zip code;post code;street address;home address
requirements: Use separate fields with autocomplete values such as address-line1, address-level2 and postal-code;Make only the parts that the user's country needs required;Support international addresses, with an optional region and flexible postcode formats;Offer postcode or address lookup, with a link to enter the address manually;Do not over-validate street names or postcodes;Put the country first when it changes the other fields;Store the address in separate parts, not one text block
done_when: Browsers autofill the whole address correctly;Users can enter an address without the lookup;Valid addresses from other countries are accepted

name: Name fields
explanation: The fields for entering a person's name, which need to work for names from every culture.
triggers: first name;last name;surname;given name;family name;middle name;full name;their name
requirements: Prefer one Full name field unless you really need separate parts;If you split it, say Given name and Family name rather than first and last;Set autocomplete to name, given-name or family-name;Accept accents, apostrophes, hyphens, spaces and non-Latin scripts;Allow long names and names with only one part;Ask separately what the user wants to be called, if you need it;Never change the case or spelling of what users type
done_when: Names with apostrophes, hyphens, accents and non-Latin scripts are accepted and saved correctly;Browsers autofill the name;Names with a single word are accepted

name: Phone number input
explanation: A field for entering a phone number, which needs to accept local and international formats.
synonyms: telephone input;international phone input;phone field;tel input
triggers: phone number;mobile number;country code;international numbers;telephone number;phone format;cell phone number
requirements: Use type=tel and autocomplete=tel;Accept spaces, dashes, brackets and a leading plus sign;Accept international numbers, with a country picker or a +country code;Store numbers in E.164 format, such as +14155550123;Validate with a maintained library such as libphonenumber, not a simple regex;Say what the number will be used for, and confirm it by text message if it matters
done_when: Numbers in common local and international formats are accepted;Phones open the number keypad;Saved numbers use one consistent format

name: Password field
explanation: The input where users type a password, with a show-password option and clear rules.
synonyms: password input;password strength meter;show password toggle;password rules
triggers: show password;show the password;hide password;reveal password;eye icon;password strength;strong password;password requirements;password must contain;confirm password
requirements: Add a Show password button that switches the field between password and text;Set autocomplete to current-password or new-password;Allow pasting, so password managers work;Show the rules before the user types and check them as they type;Accept passwords of at least 64 characters, including spaces and any symbol;Reject passwords found in lists of breached passwords;Do not ask for the new password twice when users can show it instead
done_when: Password managers can fill and save the password;Users can check what they typed with Show password;Weak or breached passwords are rejected with a clear reason

name: Email address field
explanation: A form field for typing an email address, which should accept every valid address and catch common typos.
triggers: enter their email;email typo;did you mean gmail;wrong email address;email format;type their email
requirements: Use type=email, autocomplete=email and spellcheck=false;Allow pasting, and do not ask users to type the address twice;Trim spaces before checking it;Check only the basic shape, such as name@domain, since stricter rules reject real addresses;Suggest fixes for common typos, such as gmial.com to gmail.com;Confirm the address with a link when it matters
done_when: Valid addresses with plus signs or new domains are accepted;Phones show the email keyboard;A typo such as gmial.com gets a helpful suggestion
